method.name: real-review bounded evolution
method.summary: Convert real wins and losses into bounded scoring rules, hard constraints, and protected brave behaviors before publishing.
principles: Learn from winning matches and losing matches.
Fatal risks are hard constraints, not small penalties.
Do not let defensive fixes remove star tempo, lane control, or pressure fire.
Keep one rollback baseline and one coherent hypothesis per cycle.
Use live target pools and real challenge batches for ladder evaluation; simulations are only safety checks.
Do not patch from a single fresh loss unless it is a reproducible hard constraint; cluster real replay tags before changing code.

boundedAxes.purpose: Handle active bullets, aimed shots, hidden shooters, overload lanes, skill traps, and own bombs before value actions.
requiredTests: current bullet lane is urgent
urgent bullet danger
close enemy firing lane while boosted
close overload offset firing lane
active overload remaining frames as hard offset danger
close skill trap
post-shield overload lane

boundedAxes.purpose: Use boost for valuable safe star routes without wasting it on short routes or overshooting the star.
requiredTests: valuable medium star race
opening diagonal star route
short odd-distance star route
short diagonal star route
wall-capped opening star route
opening folded route against a direct non-mobile star race
late boost for an unreachable final star
pass through a one-step star
does not cast boost while stun control reverses movement
does not reverse-walk into a stun-controlled star pin
does not boost-control a near star while already closer

boundedAxes.purpose: Preserve safe adjacent and near-star pickups before lower-value pressure, grass, or patrol actions.
requiredTests: safe adjacent star before ordinary clear fire
near-star route through star-tempo arbitration
boost star-control next to a collectible star

boundedAxes.purpose: Choose between boost, direct pickup, star control, interception, pressure, and lane exits by frame value instead of fixed-order side effects.
requiredTests: action priority in an explicit strategy pipeline
boost star-control override urgent bullet danger
keeps moving toward a close contested star
does not shield-chase a clearly lost star race
boost tempo into early pressure before far-star walking
boost confirmed shot fires before far-star value drift
late boost tempo into pressure before runtime drift
late reachable star before wall-only fire
adjacent star after recent boost instead of replanning away
recent-boost adjacent star through an active bullet
stale boost-tempo star-line hold instead of empty hold
does not convert boost tempo by entering an already aimed long lane
does not convert boost tempo by entering a two-turn long lane
boost to reach star-control position when direct race is lost
does not boost-control a stable closer star route
occupied boost star-control lane into pressure fire
favors a grass star-control station in a contested boost lane
still takes an adjacent safe star before grass control
close skill-trap tempo shot before escape

boundedAxes.purpose: Avoid corner drift, empty line holds, dead grass, and no-value fallback actions after a star window.
requiredTests: patrol does not fire dirt when it is not opening a star route
moves into nearby grass control
re-centers from a low-value edge patrol
does not spend shield on a low-value dangerous adjacent star
releases stale lead grass instead of holding empty tempo

protectedBehaviors: Keep safe immediate star pickup when no hard danger exists.
Preserve safe adjacent star pickup before ordinary fire, grass, interception, or pressure movement.
Do not cast boost while a current bullet lane is urgent.
Do not cast boost while stun or reverse control can turn acceleration into wrong-way movement.
Boost may be used for valuable safe mid or long folded star routes, especially against mobile opponents or when not leading.
When direct star race is already lost, boost may be spent to reach a star-control or pressure position instead of continuing a blind star chase.
Do not spend boost-control on stable closer or near-star routes that can already be won without acceleration.
Do not spend boost on short routes that would skip or overshoot the star.
Do not spend boost on wall-capped opening star routes whose first boosted segment ends at an edge wall before reaching the star.
Do not cast late boost for an unreachable final star that cannot be collected before the round ends.
Do not hard-veto valuable folded star routes purely because of route shape; route traces may guide scoring and overshoot guards only.
When boosted next to a star, hold or turn for a controlled pickup instead of double-stepping through it.
After boost expires next to a star, collect it before replanning away unless a real bullet, bomb, overload, hidden shooter, hard block, or point-blank enemy pickup makes the tile unsafe.
Do not reverse-walk into a stun-controlled star pin while stunned or reversed.
Boost star-control must yield to an adjacent collectible star.
Boost star-control may favor safe grass stations when they control the current star line, especially in contested star lanes.
Do not let boost star-control override urgent bullet danger.
Occupied boost star-control lines should convert into real pressure fire when the enemy gunline is clear.
Boost confirmed clear shots should fire before far-star value drift while safe adjacent stars remain protected.
Boost tempo lead should convert into early or mid/late pressure before ordinary far-star walking when no safe nearby star is available.
Late reachable stars should be collected before wall-only star-line fire.
Recent boost tempo must not keep holding an unsafe star line after it has gone stale without fire pressure.
Boost-tempo pressure and non-panic fallback movement must not step into an enemy long lane that is already aimed.
When leading by two or more stars, boost-tempo pressure must not step into a two-turn enemy long lane.
Boost skill must treat close enemy firing lanes and overload offset lanes as hard danger before value movement.
Hard danger still outranks stars, grass, pressure fire, bombs, and ordinary pathing.
Same-row or same-column gunline decisions should be resolved by frame cost before star chasing or turning in place.
Against stun or cloak skill traps, clear close pressure shots may outrank lane escape only when no current bullet or bomb hard danger exists and our shot frame is no slower than the enemy aim frame.
Do not idle in grass unless it controls a star line or pressure lane.
Lead grass control should fire from a safe pressure lane instead of holding empty tempo.
Stale lead grass control should release to pressure or value pathing instead of holding empty tempo.
Strategic grass control may outrank ordinary star pathing only when the grass controls a star line or pressure lane, and must stay bounded by safe adjacent star pickup.
Patrol must not fire dirt unless it opens the current star route.
Visual speech may add flavor, but it must not change action selection.

publishRequires: pre-publish code quality and strategy-conflict review
npm run simulate with AGENTANK_SHIELD_KEY loaded
shield-main challenge dry-run before any real challenge
explicit user confirmation before real challenge execution
stopAfter: new failure not covered by current bounded axis

driftRules: Do not convert one fresh loss directly into code unless the reviewed hard constraint is reproducible or part of a clustered failure axis.
Do not add a new tactical axis without a required regression test.
Do not optimize only from losses; preserve at least one winning behavior.
Do not publish a candidate whose protected behavior tests fail.
Do not keep raw replay dumps as persistent repo context.
Visual speech may add flavor, but it must not change action selection.
Every reviewed replay must emit preserve, fix, hard-constraint, and brave-baseline buckets.
Use real challenge batches as the decision signal; simulation results are safety checks only.
